author: Russell Brand
description:
Graham Linehan’s arrest at Heathrow over past X posts has opened a chilling question about free speech, comedy, online censorship, transgender debate, UK policing, and whether Britain is now treating forbidden jokes like real crimes. Russell Brand looks at the posts, the reaction, and the strange new world where a comedy writer can be met by police over words written online, but is this really about safety, or is something far more disturbing being normalized in plain sight? When comedians, writers, and ordinary citizens start wondering what they are still allowed to say, the free speech debate stops being theoretical and becomes impossible to ignore.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell Brand explains why he did not believe in Jesus at first, and the answer opens a much deeper question about faith, Christianity, spiritual awakening, addiction, rationality, and the hunger inside every human being that no worldly answer seems able to satisfy. Russell describes once seeing Jesus as part of a wider spiritual landscape, but what changed when reason itself seemed to run out of road? Was the craving he once chased through the world actually pointing toward something far more eternal, forbidden, and impossible to explain without faith?

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell Brand is confronted over his Christian conversion as a skeptical guest questions whether his faith, politics, and public transformation are really what they seem, but what happens next opens up a much deeper question about Christianity, MAGA, the mainstream media, faith, redemption, and whether anyone can honestly judge another person’s soul from the outside. This exchange does not feel like another clean political argument or celebrity conversion story. It feels like one of those rare moments where the comfortable script starts to break, and the question becomes whether skepticism is protecting the truth or hiding from something far bigger.
